text:
jason: thinking out loud — we should add structured shed headers + optional ticket id so clients and the console can distinguish precheck rejects (per-key/quota) from system-level circuit breaks. 429 for precheck, 503 for runtime overload, but include a consistent header set.

tara: can you sketch what headers you mean? also how should Retry-After work for prechecks? :thinking:

priya: rough proposal below. we keep 429 semantics for per-key/per-org quota prechecks and include `Retry-After` when we can compute a backoff. for node-level circuit (queue full / degraded), return 503 but emit `X-RD-SHED-REASON` and a `X-RD-SHED-TICKET` (hashed) that we can join to sampled traces.

priya: ```yaml
precheck: 
  status: 429
  headers:
    X-RD-SHED: precheck
    X-RD-SHED-REASON: quota_exceeded
    X-RD-SHED-TICKET: "rd-<hashed-ticket>"  # not full id, low-cardinality
    Retry-After: "5"  # seconds, best-effort

runtime_overload:
  status: 503
  headers:
    X-RD-SHED: node_overload
    X-RD-SHED-REASON: queue_full
    X-RD-SHED-TICKET: "rd-<hashed-ticket>"
```

liam: how do we avoid high-cardinality in telemetry if we emit tickets? hashed ticket ok, but we should sample ticket->trace linking at 0.5% by default. console can surface aggregated counts per reason and per-org shed_rate.

console-ux-amy: from UX side we want two things: a per-route "shed rate" time series (split by reason) and an explorable sample list of tickets that links to a trace record. sampling + hashed id works. also add a CTA to explain expected client behavior (retry/backoff).

dave: telemetry cost concern — please ensure tickets are hashed and that we only index ticket id when sampled. Also add a small derived metric: `rd.shed.per_org.24h` (count) so customers can see their quota pressure without us storing every ticket.

jason: agree on hashed tickets + sampling. on HTTP semantics: for precheck 429 we should return `Retry-After` (seconds) when available. if unknown, include `Retry-After: 0`? maybe better to omit and rely on `X-RD-SHED-REASON`. thoughts?

tara: prefer to include best-effort Retry-After for better client behavior. if we can't compute, return `Retry-After: 1` to avoid tight spin loops. document it clearly in the API docs and SDKs.

priya: implementation notes: router needs to attach headers at the precheck stage (fast path) and at the final rejection stage. also add `x-rd-shed-version` header so we can evolve formats without breaking clients.

jason: +1 to versioning. can we add a flag to the Dedicated/private config so customers can opt-out of exposing tickets? (some regulated customers may not want any id).

liam: yes, default on for hosted, opt-out via org config for Private. document the privacy implications.

ops-bot: notice: deploy to staging queued (sha: a1b2c3) :arrow_up_small:

deploy-bot: deployed to staging:rd-shed-headers-2024-03 :white_check_mark:

console-ux-amy: will draft mockups for the shed-rate panel and ticket explorer. will sync with priya on payload shape.

jason: next steps: PR for router + telemetry changes (RFC) — I'll open PR #342 with config + header schema. can we target staging tests this week and a gradual rollout next week? assign to me, reviewers: priya, dave, amy.

priya: i'll add e2e that asserts headers on precheck path and on queue-full path, and tests that ticket header is hashed and sampled.

dave: i'll add the telemetry cost projection and sampling defaults in the RFC.

liam: I'll stub console metrics and add the `rd.shed.*` derived metrics to the metrics service.

jason: thanks all. summary: add X-RD-SHED headers + version, use 429 for precheck with Retry-After when possible, 503 for node-level overload, hashed ticket ids + sampling, console panel for shed_rate. RFC PR #342 opened and assigned. :thumbsup:
